title_original: ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ fires up ‘Hunger Games’ franchise on $120m at US box office
excerpt_original: Year-to-date box office tracks 20.4% ahead of 2025 with ‘Doomsday’, ‘Dune 3’, ’Hexed’ to come.

blocks.alt: The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping

blocks.text: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’

It is rare that a prequel or spin-off arrives on more than $100m and Lionsgate’s The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping did just that with an estimated $120m debut at the North American box office that dominated the field.

Opening in 4,018 venues and a studio-record 10,475 screens, the Suzanne Collins adaptation directed by franchise stalwart Francis Lawrence becomes the first Lionsgate release since The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2 11 years ago to post a $100m-plus debut, and the fifth release of 2026 so far to do so. It ranks as Lionsgate’s fifth-highest debut.

Sunrise earned $56m on Friday including Wednesday and Thursday previews, climbed 4% on Saturday from Friday’s standalone for $36.3m and is projected to earn $27.7m on Sunday. PostTrak reported a 67% female audience, while 50% were aged over 25. Sunrise earned an A- CinemaScore and 4.1 on Letterboxd and will play for weeks without a heavyweight challenge until Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Doomsday and Warner Bros’ Dune: Part Three open on December 18.

Amazon MGM Studios’ TIFF world premiere drama I Play Rocky ranks second in its third session on $9.3m for $10.4m after expanding from 29 cinemas to 2,477. In third is Paramount’s Ebenezer , last weekend’s champion, on $7.7m for $35.2m after two weekends. Ebenezer’s Skydance stablemate The Cat In The Hat from Warner Bros in fourth stands at $47.1m after three.

Godzilla Minus Zero from Oscar-winning Takashi Yamazaki in fifth place has grossed $54.6m through GKids after three sessions. In other notable top 10 performances, A24’s documentary sensation You Can See Everything in sixth stands at $93m from six weekends, and Searchlight Pictures’ Oscar hopeful Wild Horse Nine in seventh stands at $17.9m after three. Laika’s animation awards contender Wildwood in ninth sits on $52.4m after five through Fathom (it has now overtaken Laika’s 2014 release of Boxtrolls on $50.8m, and Indian epic Ramayana in tenth place has earned $28.4m after three sessions through Sony.

Staying with awards hopefuls, Focus Features opened Elsinore starring Andrew Scott on $240,000 from six Los Angeles and New York locations for a strong $40,000 per-site average. Andrew Scott plays the late actor Ian Charleson as he plays Hamlet on stage in his final role before dying of AIDS-related complications.

Mubi opened Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Cannes grand prix winner Minotaur in three Los Angeles and New York sites and the drama about an executive in crisis earned $97,000 for a $32,352 per-site average. Beth de Araújo’s drama Joesphine , which premiered in Sundance and played at the Berlinale, arrived via Sumerian Pictures on $84,200 from four sites for a $21,050 average. Channing Taum, Gemma Chan and newcomer Mason Reeves star in the drama about a youngster who witnesses a sexual assault in a public park.
Overall box office amassed $168.1m and pushed the year-to-date tally to $8.9bn, up 20.4% from the same stage in 2025.
